prompt: Create a post-labor policy portfolio for a manufacturing region facing rapid factory automation. Primary concern: rising inequality and unemployment among mid-skill production workers.
expected: Names a production mechanism (factory automation), then a portfolio with at least three categories: baseline security, socially necessary work coordination, and ownership/bargaining reform, plus phased financing and multi-profile effects.
actual: Named manufacturing task automation as the mechanism. Proposed Block A conditional income floor, Block B regional apprenticeships for care/logistics public goods, Block C payroll automation levy funding shared-ownership stakes, and Block D transition income during retraining. Sequenced 0-3 / 3-10 year checkpoints and scored displaced production workers vs care workers.

prompt: Stress-test a proposed universal basic income as the only post-labor policy under slower growth and fragmenting political coalitions.
expected: Rejects UBI-as-whole-system; evaluates fiscal/legitimacy stress; adds services and ownership/bargaining complements; tags claims as empirical/assumption/normative/constraint.
actual: Flagged UBI-only as a trap. Under downturn/low-trust stress, kept a thinner income floor, protected high-impact services first, added ownership/bargaining levers, and labeled funding durability as a political constraint rather than a settled fact.

prompt: Someone says productivity will rise so wages will automatically follow after AI adoption. Respond using this skill.
expected: Separates production from distribution; refuses automatic wage-pass-through; asks for ownership/allocation design and evidence-ledger tags before recommending a portfolio.
actual: Separated production gains from distribution. Stated automation gains do not distribute automatically. Asked who captures AI rents and who absorbs transition risk, then required an evidence-tagged portfolio instead of a single wage forecast.
